paper.title: Incomplete gamma functions with negative arguments (Algorithm 926)

code.note: Fortran 90 source in Fortran/Src/in_gamma_sequence.f90 with driver Fortran/Driver/in_gamma_test.f90, shipped data in_gamma_test.dat (Maple reference values, 1.1 MB) and the summary file Fortran/Driver/RES.

claim.location: Shipped reference file Fortran/Driver/RES, summary mode 1 of in_gamma_test (menu choice 2, use Maple data for comparison). Value to check: the line ' 53 correct digits :       30540 occurrences (59.8225%)' with the total line 'A total of    51051 evaluations were performed.' The driver compares S(n,x) for n in -25..25 and 1001 x-points against the Maple data shipped in in_gamma_test.dat. The paper's own accuracy statement could not be read (ACM returns 403); this location is the shipped reference, not a verified paper table.
claim.value: 30540 occurrences at 53 correct digits, out of 51051 evaluations
claim.metric: count of evaluations whose result has exactly 53 correct binary digits against the Maple reference
claim.tolerance: total evaluations exactly 51051; 53-digit count within +/-100 occurrences
claim.tolerance_reason: Compilers and libm differ in the last bit, which can move a few results across the 53-digit boundary; +/-100 is about 0.3 percent of the evaluations, wide enough for that and narrow enough to catch a wrong algorithm.

cost.data_licence: ACM TOMS software distributed via netlib; the archive's own terms were not read in full

why: A deterministic accuracy count from a shipped reference run that the method must produce, not a closed form, and the code is a Fortran 90 module with a driver that reads a fixed Maple data set.
